findings.concern: Asymmetric error handling between the durable and legacy ports. Every durable-port call in read()/save()/clear() is wrapped in its own try/catch, but the two legacy-port calls on the fallback/degrade paths are not: `const legacyValue = legacy.read();` (line 82, read()'s migration fallback) and `legacy.write(token);` (line 109, save()'s degrade branch) call straight through. A legacy (window.localStorage) failure -- e.g. a SecurityError under a storage-blocking browser policy, or a QuotaExceededError on write -- would propagate as a rejected promise instead of degrading gracefully the way every durable-side failure already does. Concretely, this is reachable from two call sites in the diff: App.tsx's mount effect (App.tsx:30-34) consumes `readToken()` via `.then()` with no `.catch()`, so a `legacy.read()` throw would leave `authorized` stuck at `null` and strand the app on the 'Loading…' placeholder indefinitely rather than ever reaching the token screen; TokenGate's submit handler (App.tsx:66-72) awaits `saveToken(token)` with no try/catch, so a compound failure (both durable AND legacy writes rejecting) would make the Save button silently inert. Neither path is covered by the approved suite -- FakeLegacyStorage exposes no failNextReadWith()/failNextWriteWith() -- so this is NOT a suite-coherence violation; every one of the 16 pinned assertions matches the code's actual behavior exactly (independently re-derived, see reason text below). Rated low rather than medium because the trigger requires an atypical localStorage failure on the owner's own two already-in-production, mainstream, same-origin browser environments (Android Chrome + Windows PC per CON-007), which none of the plan's Risks table, the PRD's Technical Risks, or ADR-0003 anticipate -- every artifact in this phase's chain treats localStorage as the reliable pre-existing floor, never a failure mode to design around.
